## Closing lesson: tick the AC boxes ONLY -- adding prose to the description at close time breaks the attestation

S0's close was blocked twice, both times correctly, and the second block taught something worth
keeping.

BLOCK 1 -- unchecked acceptance criteria. The completion gate refused because all six '- [ ]' items
were still unticked. It offered --force; not used. Verified all six against the ADR AS MERGED on
origin/main at 85ef5ad33ada rather than against intent: Option A (decision 1) and Option C
(decision 3) recorded; the PID+heartbeat lease documented as spiked and 'rejected as unsound';
decision 4 'Root stays 60 GiB -- that is headroom, not the fix' with the measurement that 60 GiB
fills as readily as 30 and only changes how long the fuse is; per-generator alarm precedent via
rebar-gerrit-data-disk-debris; external native-GC precedents Gitaly, Sourcegraph gitserver, Bazel,
ccache, Docker overlay2/BuildKit; and the commit touching exactly three files. All six genuinely
held, so ticking them was reporting a fact, not satisfying a gate.

BLOCK 2 -- and this is the reusable lesson. Alongside ticking the boxes I appended a short
explanatory blockquote to the description. The close then failed 'stale-material', and the gate's
message is unusually precise and worth quoting:

  'its TEXT changed, and checkbox state changed too (0 -> 6 ticked), which is NOT the cause; note
   that ticking an AC checkbox is attestation-SAFE (box state is normalized out of the fingerprint),
   so a tick is never the cause.'

So: checkbox state is deliberately normalized out of the plan fingerprint precisely so a close can
tick boxes without invalidating the attestation. ANY OTHER description edit at close time does
invalidate it and forces a fresh 15-20 minute review-plan. RULE: at close, tick boxes and change
nothing else; put closing evidence in a COMMENT. Removing the 231-character note restored the text
to the reviewed baseline (6997 -> 6998 chars, a trailing newline) and cleared stale-material.

Note also the gate diagnosed the cause for me instead of just reporting staleness -- it distinguished
the text change from the tick change and pre-emptively ruled the tick out. That is a good failure
message and the reason this cost minutes rather than a wasted gate run.

REMAINING QUESTION, being tested by the third close attempt: 'review-plan --status' still reports
stale-code, because the three file_impact paths changed -- which is S0's OWN work landing. With
currency_basis=file_impact that appears to be the normal end state of every completed ticket. If the
close gate enforced stale-code, no ticket carrying file_impact could ever close without re-running
plan review, so it presumably does not. Worth confirming empirically rather than assuming, which is
what the current attempt does.
